title: Sinusoidal – A Card Game Against a Language Model You Can Rewire
tools: Godot 4 (GDScript, shaders) · Qwen3.5-2B · PyTorch steering vectors · Sparse autoencoders · PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization)
blurb: A 3D card roguelike in Godot where the opponent, a wooden automaton called the Dealer, is a real small language model (Qwen3.5-2B). Open its head and cut glowing wires, and each cut adds a steering vector to the model's activations, changing how it talks and plays.
long: Sinusoidal is a 3D card roguelike with a dark, low-resolution look: a 480×270 render, a palette shader that snaps dark colours, a swinging lamp and candles. A run is a branching map of battles, card choices and events on a parchment, with three candles as lives; the rules, 9 sigils (creature abilities) and 10 events are data-driven and covered by headless test and balance sims.

The hook is that the Dealer is a language model you can tamper with. Its head opens to show four coloured wires; each wire is a contrastive direction (the mean activation on one set of prompts minus another, at one layer), and cutting it adds that direction to the residual stream. Players are never told what a wire means and learn it by watching the Dealer change.

Sandbox switches test interpretability papers as game mechanics on the Dealer's own model. A persona gauge reads its replies against persona vectors (evil, sycophantic, paranoid and others): grafting a trait at layer 12 moved that trait's needle the most, by 5 to 12 standard deviations, in a single run. A concept-injection test found the 2B model named an injected concept 0 times in 120 pilot trials, so the 'does it notice?' mechanic stays a sandbox curiosity. A Why? ledger traces each move with occlusion of board lines and sparse-autoencoder features, and a small PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) reinforcement-learning policy lets cut wires bias the Dealer's play.
In progress, built in parallel feature tracks. The card portraits are placeholders carried over from Lantern Depths.
